title: The Renaissance
description: Artists, thinkers and inventions of Europe's rebirth, from about 1300 to 1600

questions.question: In which Italian city did the Renaissance largely begin?
questions.explanation: Florence, wealthy from banking and the wool trade and home to patrons such as the Medici, is generally seen as the Renaissance's birthplace.

questions.question: Which powerful banking family were major patrons of the arts in Florence?
questions.explanation: The Medici funded artists and scholars including Botticelli and Michelangelo. The family later produced popes and queens.

questions.question: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.explanation: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling between 1508 and 1512, including the famous 'Creation of Adam'.

questions.question: Who developed a movable-type printing press in Europe around 1440?
questions.explanation: Johannes Gutenberg's press in Mainz made books far cheaper and spread Renaissance ideas quickly. His Bible was printed around 1455.

questions.question: Who wrote 'The Prince', a treatise on political power?
questions.explanation: Machiavelli wrote 'The Prince' in 1513. Thomas More wrote 'Utopia', and Dante wrote the 'Divine Comedy' earlier, around 1308-1321.

questions.question: Which intellectual movement of the Renaissance focused on classical texts and human potential?
questions.explanation: Renaissance humanists such as Petrarch studied Greek and Roman texts and emphasized human achievement and education.

questions.question: Which astronomer proposed a heliocentric model in 'On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres' (1543)?
questions.explanation: Copernicus put the Sun at the center of the cosmos. Galileo and Kepler later supported and refined the idea.

questions.question: Who painted the 'Mona Lisa'?
questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the 'Mona Lisa' in the early 1500s. It now hangs in the Louvre in Paris.

questions.question: Which architect engineered the great dome of Florence Cathedral?
questions.explanation: Brunelleschi completed the dome in 1436 without traditional wooden centering. He is also credited with developing linear perspective.

questions.question: Which Botticelli painting shows a goddess arriving on a scallop shell?
questions.explanation: 'The Birth of Venus' (c. 1485) shows Venus arriving at the shore on a shell. 'The School of Athens' is by Raphael and 'The Last Supper' by Leonardo.
